reason: The passage, which appears to be 1 Kings 22 (the account of Ahab, Jehoshaphat, and the battle at Ramoth-gilead), contains no instance of Hebrew leaders complaining about the people. While Micaiah does prophesy that he 'saw all Israel scattered on the mountains like sheep that have no shepherd' (וַיֹּ֗אמֶר רָאִ֤יתִי אֶת־ כָּל־ יִשְׂרָאֵל֙ נְפֹצִ֣ים אֶל־ הֶהָרִ֔ים כַּצֹּ֕אן אֲשֶׁ֥ר אֵין־ לָהֶ֖ם רֹעֶ֑ה), this is a prophetic vision of consequences, not a complaint by leaders about the people's character or behavior.
